mcqs.question: In the nitrate ion (NO₃⁻) one of the N–O bonds is formed when an oxygen atom donates both electrons to nitrogen. Which of the following best identifies this coordinate covalent bond?

options.A: The N–O bond in which the oxygen atom supplies both electrons for the shared pair
options.B: The N–O bond where each atom contributes one electron
options.C: The N–O double bond present in the ion
options.D: All three N–O bonds are identical and none is coordinate

mcqs.answer: The N–O bond in which the oxygen atom supplies both electrons for the shared pair
mcqs.explanation: A coordinate (dative) covalent bond is formed when one atom provides both electrons for the shared pair. In NO₃⁻, one oxygen donates its lone pair to nitrogen, creating such a bond. Options B and C describe ordinary covalent sharing, and D is incorrect because the bonds are not all the same.

mcqs.question: Two hydrogen atoms each have one unpaired electron. They approach each other and form a molecule H₂. Which statement correctly explains the single bond formed between the two hydrogen atoms?

options.A: One hydrogen atom donates both electrons to the bond while the other contributes none
options.B: Each hydrogen atom contributes one electron, and the pair is shared between them
options.C: Electrons are transferred completely from one hydrogen to the other, creating an ionic bond
options.D: The bond involves sharing of three electron pairs

mcqs.answer: Each hydrogen atom contributes one electron, and the pair is shared between them
mcqs.explanation: A single covalent bond is the sharing of one pair of electrons, one contributed by each atom. Option A describes a coordinate bond, C describes ionic bonding, and D is impossible for hydrogen.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about double bonds reflects a common misconception?

options.A: A double bond is shorter than a comparable single bond
options.B: A double bond involves two shared pairs of electrons
options.C: A double bond is generally stronger than a single bond because more electrons are shared
options.D: The length of a double bond is exactly half that of a single bond

mcqs.answer: The length of a double bond is exactly half that of a single bond
mcqs.explanation: While double bonds are shorter than single bonds, they are not half the length; the reduction is less than 50%. Options A, B, and C are correct statements about double bonds. Option D is the misconception.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct Lewis structure for carbon dioxide (CO₂)?

options.A: C double‑bonded to each O, with two lone pairs on each O
options.B: C single‑bonded to each O, with three lone pairs on each O
options.C: C triple‑bonded to one O and single‑bonded to the other O
options.D: C with no bonds and each O bearing three bonds

mcqs.answer: C double‑bonded to each O, with two lone pairs on each O
mcqs.explanation: CO₂ follows the octet rule: carbon forms two double bonds with oxygen, giving carbon 4 bonds (8 electrons) and each oxygen 2 bonds plus two lone pairs (8 electrons). Option B violates carbon's octet, C is not the observed structure, and D is impossible.

mcqs.question: Two resonance structures of the carbonate ion (CO₃²⁻) are shown. Structure I has one C=O double bond and two C–O single bonds (each O with a –1 charge). Structure II shows three equivalent C–O bonds (all single) with each O bearing a –1 charge. Which structure gives the lower magnitude of formal charge on the central carbon atom?

options.A: Structure I with one C=O double bond
options.B: Structure II with three equivalent single bonds
options.C: Both structures give the same formal charge on carbon
options.D: Neither; carbon carries a +2 charge in both structures

mcqs.answer: Structure I with one C=O double bond
mcqs.explanation: Formal charge on carbon = valence electrons – (non‑bonding + ½ bonding). In Structure I, carbon has four bonds (8 bonding electrons), giving FC = 4 – 4 = 0. In Structure II, carbon has three single bonds (6 bonding electrons), giving FC = 4 – 3 = +1. Therefore Structure I has the lower (zero) formal charge. Options C and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds contains a coordinate (dative) covalent bond?
mcqs.explanation: In the BF₃·NH₃ adduct, the lone pair on nitrogen of NH₃ is donated to the electron‑deficient boron atom of BF₃, forming a coordinate covalent bond. The other molecules involve only ordinary covalent sharing.

mcqs.question: A single covalent bond is best described as:

options.A: The sharing of one pair of electrons between two atoms
options.B: The complete transfer of two electrons from one atom to another
options.C: The sharing of two pairs of electrons between two atoms
options.D: A bond formed without any electron sharing

mcqs.answer: The sharing of one pair of electrons between two atoms
mcqs.explanation: A single bond involves one shared electron pair, one contributed by each atom. Option B describes ionic bonding, C describes a double bond, and D is incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement about multiple (double or triple) covalent bonds is correct?

options.A: Multiple bonds involve the sharing of more than one pair of electrons between the same two atoms
options.B: Multiple bonds are always ionic in nature
options.C: Multiple bonds have longer bond lengths than corresponding single bonds
options.D: Multiple bonds are formed when only one atom supplies all the shared electrons

mcqs.answer: Multiple bonds involve the sharing of more than one pair of electrons between the same two atoms
mcqs.explanation: A double bond shares two electron pairs, a triple bond shares three. This increases bond strength and shortens bond length compared to a single bond. Options B, C, and D are false.
